impact.rationale: The Go-only patch introduces a durable scheduler sidecar, opaque attempt authority, persistent reservations, automated worker retries, API views, and changes shared subscription and runtime paths. The feature is default-off, but defects in the enabled path can affect durable state, admission capacity, or service lifetime.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The seven v5 delta paths are narrowly targeted and the four previously deterministic defects are source-closed, but the candidate has not been compiled, formatted, race-tested, or executed on Linux and still spans 24 Go afterimages.

regressionProtection.rationale: Source review found dedicated tests for every mutator's definite pre-rename cut, detached outward reservations, high-water truth-table rejection, exact-stage retry, authorization revalidation, cancellation, read visibility, manual TryLock behavior, and uncertain-commit non-retry. These tests are authored but were not run.

recoverability.rationale: The feature remains default-off and the v5 source is isolated as a reversible 24-path patch. Enabled deployments write a separately versioned sidecar and main-store records, so rollback requires controlled state-aware handling rather than a blind source revert.

confidence.rationale: Confidence is high for the scoped source conclusion because patch identities, all 24 afterimages, reverse application, the seven-path v4-to-v5 delta, the relevant production call chains, and the targeted test bodies were independently inspected. Runtime confidence remains intentionally withheld.

applicability.rationale: The patch directly modifies the P207A refresh sidecar and production subscription worker paths named in the review request; the v5 delta specifically addresses the four confirmed v4 blockers.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Without the v5 changes, a definite pre-rename sidecar failure can mutate live state, leaked reservation pointers can mutate authority-bearing capacity state, known-not-committed stages terminate the worker/runtime, and persisted positive attempt sequences below a ledger high-water can reopen.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A definite pre-rename persistence failure must leave the authoritative live snapshot and durable bytes unchanged, and the same capability must be able to retry the same writer.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A shallow copy shares Refreshes or Reservation storage; a mutation before disk.write returns not-committed changes s.state and makes the retry skip or conflict.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Every mutator builds from cloneRefreshSnapshot, persist encodes another owned clone, assigns s.state only after a successful writer return, and capability flags are changed only after successful persistence.

materialBoundaries.invariant: No list, read, live-claim, recovery-claim, or completion return may expose a pointer into the sidecar-owned Reservation graph.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: chengwang/internal/subscription/refresh.go: cloneRefreshView, detachRefreshView, Refreshes, SnapshotRefreshes, claim, Complete
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A caller mutates returned Reservation.Bytes or slot fields and changes subsequent capacity or authorization decisions without persistence.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: All outward views deep-copy Reservation and remove Lease and transient storage fields; live or recovery claims add only a source-issued process-local lease to the detached copy.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Only a RefreshStore persist whose writer reports that rename did not occur may authorize exact-stage retry; encode, validation, store usability, and uncertain post-rename failures must not be retried.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A parse, canonical-validation, poisoned-store, or uncertain-commit error is reclassified as known-not-committed and repeats authority or network work.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: persist returns the dedicated sentinel only on disk.write's false commit-certainty result; errors before disk.write pass through, true uncertainty poisons and returns CodeCommitUncertain, and the worker retries only errors.Is with the dedicated sentinel.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A known-not-committed bind, reservation, or completion write must remain on the same lease and stage, without repeating Fetch, Import, main-store mutation, or audit work, while cancellation safely stops with Running authority retained.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: finishRefresh returns the first definite write error to RunRefresh, causing the runtime worker to exit or a later loop to reacquire and replay external work.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: retryRefreshStoreStage encloses only the local sidecar call at checkpoint, observe, reconcile, claim, bind, reservation, and complete; external effects remain outside each closure, the same arguments and lease are retained, and context cancellation exits the backoff loop.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Retry must not bypass fresh source-owned authorization, duplicate external work, block manual goroutines indefinitely, or hide safe pending state from reads.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: chengwang/internal/subscriptionctl/service.go: Execute and executeRefreshLocked; refresh.go read projections
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A long storage backoff queues manual writes behind a blocking mutex, or stale identity remains authorized when the bind retry eventually succeeds.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Feature-on manual Execute uses TryLock, reads use non-mutating detached snapshots with bounded pending metadata, and CurrentPrincipal plus refreshPrincipalCurrent are checked before Fetch and again before Import.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Every persisted positive AttemptSequence must equal the matching source ledger LastIssuedSequence; zero remains limited to the existing idle and sequence-exhausted blocked forms.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A running, blocked, or unknown record with a lower positive sequence reopens and permits a stale attempt identity after a higher sequence was issued.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The validator rejects any positive sequence unequal to the ledger high-water and separately retains producer-state and global LastSequence checks.
